label: Why sound
detail: Radio fades within a few meters of seawater, so underwater links use sound, at about 1500 m/s. A question and answer across 1.5 km take two seconds before anyone has said anything.

label: How I got the research post
detail: Dr. Aldo Duarte recommended me for the ONR project based on the software-defined radio work in his communications design course.

label: One unit, wrong by a thousand
detail: bellhopSim stored the seabed density in g/cm³, but arlpy expects kg/m³. BELLHOP saw a bottom far lighter than water that reflected almost without loss.

label: Why water matters
detail: My little brother drowned in our backyard pool at 14 months old. He survived. Because of ADAM is everything we wish we'd known.

label: Tone pairs and chips
detail: JANUS, the NATO standard for underwater modems, hops across 13 tone pairs, one 6.25 ms chip at a time. The playground hops in its own order, not the standard's.
